four_layer_diagnosis.measurement: UNDER-INSTRUMENTED for the conclusion the summary invites, and blind in a specific way. The headline recovery_ratio_median of 0.999379 reads as near-perfect stability but is the centre of two opposite-direction pairs: both L3->L5 runs recover ABOVE 1 (1.0987, 1.0702) and both L5->L3 runs BELOW 1 (0.7919, 0.9285); stream_corr moves oppositely by direction too (L3->L5 falls, L5->L3 rises 4-6x). The pooled median is therefore a cancellation of a directional split rather than a converged central value. With n=2 per direction this is a PATTERN WORTH TESTING, not an established asymmetry -- four runs cannot separate a real direction effect from layout-pair noise. The point that survives regardless is procedural: a pilot whose declared job is to ANCHOR a recovery threshold should report the per-direction pairs, because the pooled statistic destroys exactly the structure an anchor would need. Separately, n_steps_measured is 407-769 against a docstring-nominal 8000/6000 because each eval episode breaks on env done; neither manifest nor docstring reconciles this.

learning_extracted: A run can be recorded as supporting evidence for a claim without ever having had a criterion. 'verdict: PASS' here is an unconditional literal print (driver:508) whose stated purpose is to advance the runner's progress bar. The author qualified it in the driver docstring and the queue note -- neither of which any downstream consumer reads. A progress token and a scientific verdict must not share a wire format; if a diagnostic must emit a verdict line for the runner, it should emit one that cannot be mistaken for a result.

THE INDEXER READS THE RUNNER SUMMARY, NOT THE RUN-PACK MANIFEST -- and this is the fact that determines the remedy. No indexer glob reaches <exp>/<run_id>/manifest.json; the run's own INDEX.md links 'manifest' to v3_exq_472_..._output.json, whose keys are exactly claim_ids / experiment_purpose / output_files / run_id / status. The rich manifest beside it -- the one that declares evidence_direction 'diagnostic' and carries the design, per-run numbers and note -- is invisible to the index. Any remedy aimed at the manifest's contents is aimed at a file nothing reads.

The phantom 'supports' is a THREE-CONDITION conjunction and the middle one is an absence, not a bad value. (1) status 'DIAGNOSTIC' is outside _DERIVED_STATUSES so final_status collapses to PASS. (2) the file read carries NO evidence_direction key at all, so _normalize_direction(None) returns 'unknown' -- not because 'diagnostic' is disallowed, which was this autopsy's own first and wrong reading. (3) direction_explicitly_set keys on the presence of an evidence_direction_note (build_experiment_indexes.py:1871), not on evidence_direction, so the guard against auto-inference never engages. Lines 3519-3520 then infer 'supports' from the collapsed PASS.

The cheapest correct fix is the one the run already gives the indexer for free: experiment_purpose. That key IS present in the file the indexer reads, and it says 'diagnostic'. The direction inference at 3519-3520 consults final_status but not experiment_purpose, so it converts a declared diagnostic into positive evidence. Gating that inference on experiment_purpose != 'diagnostic' fixes this class at the point where the information already exists -- unlike extending _normalize_direction (which cannot see a key that is absent), hand-editing the derived claim_evidence row (regenerated by the next governance.sh), or widening _DERIVED_STATUSES alone (which would flip the phantom to 'weakens' rather than remove it).

The blast radius is one row, and saying so precisely matters more than the alarm. Across the runs carrying a non-standard explicit manifest status, 69 claim_evidence rows are produced and exactly ONE -- this one -- reads 'supports'; 65 of 69 are scoring_excluded, and the 4 that are not all read 'mixed'. Every other affected run declares a direction that survives normalisation intact. (The RUN count is scan-dependent, 35-40, because a run can appear in several files with different status keys; the row-level figures are stable across scans.) The status->PASS collapse is real and broad; only the direction inference manufactures a positive, and only where the direction key is also missing.

The harm here is a mislabel, not a weighting error -- state it at that strength and no higher. The row carries scoring_excluded 'diagnostic_probe' and adjudication 'unverified', and it is genuinely inert on every scored register: SD-011's direction_counts, pass_runs and posterior all exclude it, SD-011 is absent from the gap register, and it appears nowhere in promotion_demotion_recommendations. Its only visible surface is pending_review.md, by design. It is worth fixing because it misleads a human reader and because it is a landmine if scoring_excluded is ever relaxed -- not because it is currently weighting a claim.

A median can be a cancellation. recovery_ratio_median 0.999379 reads as textbook stability and is the midpoint of two opposite-direction pairs. For a pilot whose declared job is to anchor a downstream recovery threshold, that is the one summary statistic that destroys the information the anchor needs -- report the per-direction pairs. (With n=2 per direction the split itself is suggestive only.)

Check what a proposal's status field actually says before inferring that downstream work never happened. This autopsy's first draft argued the cancellation-artifact anchor never propagated because EXP-0090 'has no executed run or driver'. EXP-0090 is in fact recorded status 'executed', executed_by V3-EXQ-198 -- a run 20 days BEFORE the pilot written to anchor it. The conclusion (the anchor never propagated) survives, because that earlier run carries no C7 threshold; the stated reason did not.
